questiontext.text:
Goal

A crayfish boat and the wharf communicate by radio, one catch at a time. Neither end can store a message until the other is ready to receive it.

Read
  • Channel types. Read the paragraph about make and the following paragraph. For a channel without capacity, what must both sides do before a send succeeds? In what order do values arrive?
  • Receive operator. Read the first paragraph and four examples. How does code receive a channel value? What happens if no value is available?
Required: chan, <-
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • A goroutine is a function that runs alongside its caller rather than after it. The grader starts send in a goroutine, so send and take run at the same time.
  • In the Channel types section, find the three example declarations under ChannelType, then compare them with the four examples under Receive operator. Which side of the operator does the channel name sit on in each?

testcode.text: ch := make(chan string) go send([]string{"paua", "kina"}, ch) fmt.Println(take(2, ch))
ch := make(chan string) go send([]string{"toheroa"}, ch) fmt.Println(take(1, ch))
ch := make(chan string) go send([]string{"kina", "paua", "kina", "cockle", "pipi", "kina"}, ch) fmt.Println(take(6, ch))
ch := make(chan string) go send([]string{"pipi", "tuatua", "cockle"}, ch) fmt.Println(take(0, ch))

questiontext.text:
Goal

A bakery passes each loaf through a hatch to a waiting queue. After the final loaf, the baker closes the hatch. The queue must still collect every loaf that already passed through.

Read
  • close. Read all four sentences. Who should call it? Who should not? What does a two-value receive report after closure?
  • For statements with range clause. Find the channel row and the following channel paragraph. What stops a range loop over a channel?
  • Channel types. Read the ChannelType production and three examples. What differs between the declarations? Which channel can only receive?
Required: close
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • A range over a channel keeps going until one call records that no more values will be sent. The builtin page names that call and says which side should make it.
  • Check the capacity paragraph in Channel types. What must both sides do before an unbuffered send completes? What else must be running when bake sends?

testcode.text: hatch := bake([]string{"rye", "oat"}) first, ok1 := <-hatch second, ok2 := <-hatch third, ok3 := <-hatch fmt.Printf("%q %v %q %v %q %v\n", first, ok1, second, ok2, third, ok3)

questiontext.text:
Goal

A committee receives motions until the chair rings a bell to end the meeting. The clerk also needs to report whether a motion is available now without waiting for another one.

Read
  • Select statements. Read the numbered steps. If several communications can proceed, which case runs? If none can proceed, which case runs?
  • Receive operator. Read about closed channels and the two-result assignment form. Does receiving from a closed channel wait? What does the second result mean?
Required: select
Stuck? Two nudges inside
  • Read step two under Select statements. Which case in poll is the fallback?
  • Find the two-result assignment form under Receive operator. What does its boolean report? For sit, what should a select without a default do after recording each motion?

testcode.text: tray := make(chan string, 1) tray <- "levy" first, ok1 := poll(tray) second, ok2 := poll(tray) fmt.Printf("%q %v %q %v\n", first, ok1, second, ok2)
motions := make(chan string) done := make(chan struct{}) go func() { motions <- "levy" motions <- "bylaw" close(done) }() fmt.Println(sit(motions, done))
shut := make(chan string) close(shut) value, ok := poll(shut) fmt.Printf("%q %v\n", value, ok)
motions := make(chan string) done := make(chan struct{}) close(done) fmt.Println(sit(motions, done))
